posts.title: Small habits compound
posts.body:
Getting 1% better each day adds up to a lot over a year.
- Tiny changes look trivial on any single day.
- Over months they stack into large differences.
👉 Start with a habit you can do in two minutes.

posts.title: Schedule your deep work
posts.body:
Focus is a skill, and it needs a plan.
- Block fixed hours for hard thinking.
- Keep shallow tasks in a separate slot.
👉 Protect one block a day before anything else.

posts.title: System 1 and System 2
posts.body:
Fast intuition is useful, and it is also where biases come from.
- System 1 answers quickly and by feel.
- System 2 is slow and only engages when needed.
👉 When a decision feels too easy, slow down.

posts.title: Don't live with broken windows
posts.body:
Small neglect invites bigger neglect. Fix the small thing today.
👉 Leave the code a little better than you found it.

posts.title: Rate limiter: where to put it
posts.body:
A rate limiter protects services from too many requests. Place it deliberately.
- Client side: cheap, but easy to bypass.
- Server or gateway: the usual choice.
- Middleware in the service: fine for one service.
👉 Most teams start at the API gateway.

posts.title: Back-of-envelope estimates
posts.body:
Estimates help you see which parts of a design will be hard.
- Users x requests per user gives QPS.
- Peak is usually 2–3x average.
👉 Round the numbers. Precision is not the point.

posts.title: Consistent hashing
posts.body:
Adding or removing a cache node should not remap every key.
- Place nodes and keys on a ring.
- Each key goes to the next node clockwise.
👉 Virtual nodes spread the load more evenly.

posts.title: Leader-follower replication
posts.body:
Replication keeps copies of data on several machines.
- Writes go to the leader.
- Followers replicate the change log.
👉 Ask yourself what happens when the leader dies.

posts.title: Designing a URL shortener
posts.body:
A small system that shows the core trade-offs of storage, IDs, and reads.
👉 Swipe through the walkthrough.

slides.title: The problem
slides.body: Turn a long URL into a short code and redirect when it is opened.

slides.title: Scale estimate
slides.body:
- 100M new URLs a month
- Read-heavy: about 100:1 reads to writes

slides.title: Generating the code
slides.body: Options: hash the URL, use a counter with base62, or pre-generate keys.

slides.title: Storage and reads
slides.body: A key-value store fits. Cache hot codes in front of it.

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: **Read-heavy systems** pay off when you cache the hot path first.

posts.title: Strategy pattern in one example
posts.body:
Swap an algorithm without changing the code that uses it.
- Define an interface for the behavior.
- Inject the concrete strategy.
👉 Think of payment methods or pricing rules.
posts.code:
class Checkout:
    def __init__(self, pricing): self.pricing = pricing

posts.title: LRU cache: the two structures
posts.body:
Get and put both need O(1).
- A hash map finds the node.
- A doubly linked list tracks recency.
👉 Evict from the tail, move hits to the head.

posts.title: Parking lot: model the spots
posts.body:
Start with the entities before you write classes.
- Lot, Level, Spot, Vehicle, Ticket.
- Spot size matches vehicle size.
👉 Keep allocation logic out of the Vehicle class.

posts.title: Reflection: let the model check its work
posts.body:
A second pass can catch errors the first pass missed.
- Generate a draft.
- Critique it against clear criteria.
- Revise.
👉 Only useful when the critique has a concrete rubric.

posts.title: RAG starts with chunking
posts.body:
Retrieval quality depends on how you split documents.
- Too big: the answer gets diluted.
- Too small: the context gets lost.
👉 Measure retrieval hit rate before you tune the prompt.

posts.title: Why the KV cache matters
posts.body:
During decoding, past keys and values are reused instead of recomputed.
- Saves compute per generated token.
- Costs memory that grows with context length.
👉 Long context is often limited by memory, not compute.

posts.title: How ViT sees an image
posts.body:
A vision transformer treats an image as a sequence of patches.
- Split the image into fixed-size patches.
- Flatten each patch and project it to a vector.
👉 Patch size trades detail for sequence length.
